r.정치 구도: Chile has a presidential system with four-year terms and no immediate re-election. After the military government that seized power in a 1973 coup stepped down in 1990, the center-left and center-right alternated in office and Chile was regarded as the most stable democracy in South America. The constitution, though, is still the 1980 text written under military rule, amended many times. Protests that began over a subway fare rise in 2019 grew into anger at inequality and led to a decision to write a new one, but a left-leaning draft in 2022 and a right-leaning draft in 2023 were both rejected in referendums, so the old text stays. Meanwhile voters' attention shifted to crime and irregular migration. A left-wing government won in 2021, and in the December 2025 runoff a hard-right candidate won and took office in March 2026. The new government dug trenches and put up fences on the northern border and began deportation flights. But the right holds 76 of the 155 seats in the lower house, short of a majority, and its economic reform cutting corporate tax passed only narrowly in August 2026.

t.why: About a quarter of the world's mined copper comes from Chile. Copper goes into power lines, electric cars and data centers, so a strike or a tax debate at Chilean mines moves the world price. It is also the second-largest producer of lithium for batteries, after Australia. China buys most of both, and the United States is discussing a critical minerals deal with Chile, which leaves it balancing between the two. On lithium the state is tightening its grip. A company combining the Atacama salt flat operations of state copper miner Codelco and private producer SQM completed its legal steps in January 2026, and Codelco takes over management from 2031. Chile is an open economy with free trade agreements with dozens of countries and is a member of the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership. It argued for decades with Bolivia over the coast it took in the 19th-century War of the Pacific, and in 2018 the International Court of Justice ruled that Chile has no obligation to negotiate. Punta Arenas in the far south is a gateway to Antarctica.
t.rel: A country more than 4,000 km long from north to south. Bolivia, which says it lost its coastline to Chile in a 19th-century war, has long demanded access to the sea.
t.korea: In 1949 Chile was the first South American country to recognize the Republic of Korea, and the two established diplomatic relations in 1962. South Korea's first free trade agreement was with Chile. After it took effect in April 2004, Chilean grapes and wine became common in Korean shops and trade between the two roughly quadrupled. South Korea sells cars and buys copper and lithium carbonate, which Korean battery makers use to produce cathode materials. Talks to update the agreement began in 2018 and then stalled, until a summit in July 2026 agreed to push ahead again and signed a memorandum on minerals cooperation. Researchers heading to South Korea's King Sejong Station in Antarctica travel through Punta Arenas.
t.know: The Atacama Desert is the driest place on Earth outside the poles, so many of the world's big observatories are there.
etext: Big mines cluster in the Atacama Desert in the north, including Escondida, the largest copper mine in the world. Codelco, created by nationalization in 1971, mines alongside foreign companies. The mines are old and the share of copper in the ore is falling, and because the desert is short of water, seawater is desalinated and pumped up the mountains.

On the Atacama salt flat, lithium comes from brine pumped up and dried in the sun, which costs less than crushing rock as Australia does. In 2023 the government set out a strategy under which the state takes majority stakes in new lithium ventures, and the Codelco-SQM company is its first result.

Being in the southern hemisphere, Chile ships fruit when the north is in winter. Cherries became a major export as a Lunar New Year gift in China, and grapes, wine and pulp sell well too. Its salmon farming is second only to Norway's.

Since the 2000s Chile has followed a fiscal rule that saves copper windfalls in sovereign wealth funds and draws on them in bad years. The individual-account pension system introduced in 1981 was copied by many countries, but low payouts caused wide discontent, and a 2025 reform made employers contribute as well.

Copper is about half of exports, so growth and the exchange rate move with the copper price and the Chinese economy. Income inequality is high, and growth has slowed since the mid-2010s. Complaints that mine and power plant permits take years are widespread, and the government that took office in 2026 has set out to shorten the process.
